change: the five cyber practice spokes stop calling the unit exam 'the full unit test', and get the course's own look instead of a second design system
_context: Three questions from Tanner about /pages/ap-cybersecurity-unit-1-practice.
The third one, whether the linking is any good, needed no change: all 35
internal links answer 200, the asset list matches the canonical data, and the
page is reachable from the umbrella and from the unit study page. The other
two did.
1. THE EXAM CARD SAID SOMETHING FALSE. It read 'Unit exam' / 'The full unit
test, once you have done the rest'. The online unit exam is not the
instrument a teacher grades: docs/cyber-unit1-bundle-vs-online.md and
docs/cyber-unit-tests-availability.md compared all five against the paper
bundle item by item, zero shared items, highest similarity 0.24. Re-measured
2026-09-06 against the five server-side lesson quizzes as well: zero exact
stems, highest token overlap 0.15. So it earns a place on a practice page,
and the sentence was false in the direction that costs a teacher.
2. 'NOT STYLED' HAS A MECHANISM AND IT IS ONE LINE OF THEME CSS. The theme
sets html{font-size:calc(var(--font-body-scale) * 62.5%)}, so every rem in
these bodies rendered at about ten pixels. The lede asked for 1.05rem and got
10.5px while the paragraph under it, having no font-size, inherited 16px, so
the page's summary line was smaller than its body text. Valid CSS, parses,
serves, wrong by a factor the stylesheet never mentions.
Measured on the live bodies the same day: ucnav, the purple unit rail, appears
29 times on ap-cyber-unit-1-exam and 52 on a lesson quiz, and zero times on
any of the five spokes. So did Georgia and the gradient hero.
3. THE ONLY STRUCTURED DATA ON THE PAGE NAMED THE WRONG COURSE. The theme
emits one BreadcrumbList per page with AP Computer Science A hardcoded as
item 2. Every real cyber page answers it with its own; these five carried
none, so the CSA claim stood unopposed on an AP Cybersecurity page.
WHY THE LIVE CHECK IS NOT ABOUT THIS DEPLOY. Merging ships the repo to
Railway, and nothing here is on the server render path: this is a generator,
a checker, a smoke suite, a verifier, a run note and a CSV. The pages change
when the Matrixify sheet is imported, which is a separate human step. So the
live check below closes on the IMPORT rather than on the deploy, and saying
otherwise would be the same defect as a live check asserting something that
was already true.

checks.name: the spoke bodies, the sheet, and thirteen mutations one rule at a time
the sibling package still validates, including the four mutations this branch nearly disabled
checks._why: Adding a class to the Keep going heading made four of its sixteen mutations match nothing, and the suite reported four RULES as missed. The anchor is class-tolerant now and an inert case fails as itself.
checks.expect: every one caught by the rule that claims it

checks.name: the sheet clears the Matrixify preflight
a second implementation reaches the same conclusions from the raw CSV and the live bodies
checks._why: Python, sharing no code with the generator: its own CSV reader, its own idea of what the page should say, and no import of the JS spec or of spokeBody. The link-loss guard in particular is re-derived by set difference on the two raw files rather than from what the generator believed it preserved. Proved not hollow by mutating the SHEET five ways (unmark the exam card, put a rem back, restore the false claim, name the CSA hub, drop a link); all five go red.
checks.expect: OK - 82 checks re-derived from the sheet and the live bodies, independently of the generator

checks.name: THE ONE THAT WAS ACTUALLY HOLLOW: test for the class as a substring instead of on the element
checks._why: This is how the check shipped in its first cut. Every one of these bodies defines .grp--exam in its own stylesheet a few hundred bytes above the card, so includes('grp--exam') is true whether or not the div carries the modifier. Stripping it off the element left the suite green. Caught in the same hour it was written, which is the only reason it is a comment rather than a live defect.
checks.expect_failure: "exam card not marked apart" was not caught at all

checks.name: stop refusing a MERGE that drops a link the live page has
checks._why: The single most costly thing this sheet could do. A MERGE republishes the whole Body HTML cell, so a link that is not in the new body stops existing on the live page, silently.
checks.expect_failure: "link loss" was not caught at all

checks.name: stop requiring the sentence that says the exam is a different instrument
checks._why: The point of the change. Without this the card can go back to reading like the graded test and nothing notices.
checks.find: if (!/not the questions on the test your teacher grades/.test(next)) {
checks.expect_failure: "exam disclaimer removed" was not caught at all

checks.name: stop refusing rem, the thing that made the page look unstyled
checks._why: Invisible in review: rem is valid CSS and the 62.5% root is in the theme rather than in this body, so the only way to catch a regression is mechanically.
checks.expect_failure: "rem sneaks back in" was not caught at all

checks.name: let the page name the CSA course in its own breadcrumb
checks._why: The defect being fixed, pointed back at itself: a spoke that emits a BreadcrumbList naming ap-csa-exam-prep is worse than emitting none, because it agrees with the theme's wrong claim in the page's own voice.
checks.expect_failure: "breadcrumb names the CSA course" was not caught at all

checks.name: let a mutation that changes no bytes count as a passing rule
checks._why: The sibling suite's failure mode this branch hit. Four of its mutations spliced against a literal heading tag, the heading grew a class, the replacements matched nothing, and four RULES were reported as missed. A mutation that does not mutate has to fail as itself, because that finding and a hollow rule send you to opposite ends of the repo. The gate refused the first version of THIS check, correctly: as a bare `if` in the loop the guard was unreachable, since every case does mutate, so deleting it changed no verdict. It is a named function asserted both ways now, which is what makes it breakable.

checks.name: the five spokes serve the new body, after the Matrixify import
checks._why: DEFERRED UNTIL THE IMPORT, not until the deploy: nothing in this change is on the server render path. Measured before the import: 5 passed, 36 failed. The 36 are exactly what the import flips. The 5 that pass are the asset-link counts, which are true on both sides and are the no-loss guard rather than the change.

not_covered: Whether the five unit exams should be public practice or premium assessment. Board 228 noindexed them on tier-3 reasoning, and the spoke is indexed, links straight to them, and calls the set 'Free and auto-scored'. That is a positioning decision and this pass deliberately did not make it. Labelling them honestly is right under either answer.

The Unit 3 exam key. Answering B twenty times scores 16 of 20 and there is no D anywhere in the key. Found 2026-09-01, unchanged on the body served today, and a different page from the ones this sheet touches.
The theme's head BreadcrumbList, which names AP Computer Science A on every page of every course. Theme work, and board 148 owns the neighbouring liquid problem.
The em-dashes in the exam pages' own hero copy. Those are page bodies this package does not own; rewriting them is its own sheet.
Whether the restyle helps. The spokes went live 2026-09-04, board 227 is already watching them for practice-keyword cannibalisation, and there is no baseline for a look.
